correctness.rationale: For theta>1 and a>0, block triangular reduction separates a quasinilpotent positive block and a compact dilation-integral negative block c K_q. Exact principal minors and a dominated finite determinant limit produce E(q,-z). Compact spectral convergence and the known simple real zeros prove the full nonzero simple positive spectrum. Unitary multiplication by h transfers the negative-block spectrum to the Doob Q on weighted L2, and the spectral radius formula gives the sharp modal norm-root rate. Root asymptotics and product factorization prove large-coupling scaling and three finite modal power sums. Packaged rational minor and numerical checks passed; proofs are analytic and prior zero facts are credited.

value.rationale: Completing all nonzero modes and deriving the exact worst-mode weighted-L2 relaxation for a natural conditioned MA(1) process fills a structural gap left by principal persistence estimates and a scalar generating function. The universal rate relative to innovation asymmetry and the large-expansion 1/(2 theta) scale are natural measurable consequences, without conflating spectral relaxation and uniform total-variation mixing.
